answer: The strongest lever is simple: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because jade only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, sparrow is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any grove approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
